the PY motifs of Epstein-Barr virus latent membrane protein 2a (LMP2a) regulate the phosphorylation status of LMP2a and associated proteins, and that LMP2a PY motif mutants still exhibit a block in BCR signal transduction.

LMP2A binds Nedd4 family members AIP4, Nedd4 and WWP2/Aip2, which regulate the protein stability of the BCR-associated protein, Lyn, and the phosphorylation of LMP1 and LMP2A in EBV-transforming LCLs.
the LMP2 PY motifs play an important role in the regulation of LMP2 protein stability and phosphorylation of LMP-associated proteins.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of LMP2-associated proteins by the LMP PY motifs and the role of LMP2 PY motifs in EB virus-induced B cell immortalization.
the role of the PY motifs in the amino-terminal domain of LMP2a in EBV-infector lymphocytes.
the role of LMP2 in EBV infection, specifically in the regulation of LMP2-associated proteins, including Lyn, which is important in the regulation of the B-cell receptor signal transduction pathway.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the LMP2 PY motifs regulate LMP2 phosphorylation and Lyn degradation and that this regulation is important in BCR signaling and LCL survival.
PY motifs of LMP2As are required to maintain a balance of protein stability and phosphorylation of LMP-associated proteins, but not for EBV immortalization of B cells.

LMP2A-mediated regulation of Lyn activity is critical for BCR signal transduction and that LMP2As PY motifs are important in regulating protein stability and the phosphorylation of LMP1-associated proteins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
LMP2A is a key regulator of BCR signaling in LCLs through its association with the PY motifs of AIP4, which is required for Lyn degradation.
LMP2A is a key player in the regulation of LMP1 and BCR signal transduction.
LMP2A is a substrate of the Nedd4 family of E3s and that the LMP2 PY motifs regulate the stability of LMP2-associated proteins.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the PY motifs of LMP2a are involved in regulating protein phosphorylation and stability of LMP2-associated proteins, which are important for EBV-mediated BCR signal transduction.
the PY motifs of LMP2a are involved in the phosphorylation and degradation of Lyn.
the LMP2 PY motifs play a role in regulating the phosphorylation of LMPA and Lyn, which in turn affects phosphorylation of other proteins, such as Syk and the unknown 60-kDa and 120-kDa proteins.
